role.altitude: The appliance repairer keeps diagnosing at the customer's home, talking with customers and repairing; writing bills by hand, calling ahead for model numbers and hunting for the right manual shrink.
skills_to_grow: Recording time, parts and findings in the work order app during the visit
role.ambitious_version: A repairer who arrives with the right part because the model and fault were known before leaving.

tasks.short: Work out the bill from time and parts, explain it to the customer, collect payment, send the receipt and have the paid bill in the accounts.

steps.what: Repairer works out the bill for repair work: call-out fee, labour and parts
Repairer explains the final bill to the customer and agrees it
Repairer collects payment by card or cash
Repairer writes the receipt and gives it to the customer
Bookkeeper types the paid bills from the invoice book into the accounts

approvals.approved_version: the bill as explained to and agreed with the customer in s2, with the payment recorded in s3

tasks.design: The work order app prices the visit from the repairer's own start and stop taps and the parts scanned during the job, with the company's rates for call-out, labour and travel zones. The repairer explains the bill and the customer agrees it, then pays on a card terminal linked to the work order, or by payment link. The receipt goes to the customer's e-mail from the app, and paid bills post to the accounting package through the work order link, so nobody types the invoice book.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bills were written in a paper invoice book and typed in at the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order apps that price jobs, take card payments and post to accounting.
tasks.still_hard: Customers who dispute the call-out fee when nothing could be fixed.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a bill so the customer feels treated fairly.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and typing; the conversation about the bill stays.

reach.learn: Whether posted bills end end-of-month catch-up.

evidence.claim: A Dutch work order platform covers quote to invoice for installers, with links to accounting packages.
A fibre network operator reports about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports (vendor case, period not stated).
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the finished job to the paid bill in the accounts; debt collection is outside.
Input contract for s1: start and stop times tapped by the repairer and parts scanned from van stock during the job, on about 85% of jobs; the rest are priced by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s5: the work order app's link to the accounting package.
Explaining the bill keeps its full time; bookkeeper time is outside the repairer's savings.
unknowns: Share of customers who pay on the spot.
research_questions: Do unpaid bills fall with payment links?

already_counted.description: Repairer corrects bills for jobs with forgotten taps or unscanned parts.

incremental.description: Repairer keeps the card terminal charged and paired.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many cash customers and unscanned parts; high: card payments and stock parts on most jobs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run the appliance, observe and examine appliances during operation to detect malfunctions such as loose parts or leaking fluid, read error codes and note findings.

steps.what: Repairer runs the appliance through its program
Repairer observes and examines the appliance during operation for loose parts, noises or leaking fluid
Repairer reads error codes from the display or service mode and looks up their meaning
Repairer notes the findings in the work order

tasks.design: Running and examining the appliance stay fully with the repairer. Error code meanings per brand are in a lookup in the work order app, and findings are spoken into a voice note that is turned into text and a suggested fault code, which the repairer confirms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written on paper after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order apps that transcribe voice memos into the order.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults that do not show during the visit.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a bearing that is about to go.

reach.learn: Whether coded findings help order the right part for the return visit.

evidence.claim: A maintenance app transcribes voice memos into the work order.
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: examining the running appliance; the repair is outside.
Input contract for s3: error code lists per brand loaded in the app by the office from manufacturers' service information.
Input contract for s4: the repairer's own voice note; no customer is recorded.
Running and observing keep their full time.
s4 is part of recording repair work, which sibling task 49-9031.00:13795 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: Brands covered by the error code lookup.
research_questions: Are findings more complete when spoken?

already_counted.description: Repairer checks the transcribed findings and code.

incremental.description: Repairer reports wrong code meanings to the office.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older appliances without error codes; high: modern appliances with many codes and long findings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the customer describe the fault and model when booking, have the work order created, read it, call the customer ahead only when needed, and talk to the customer on site to establish the nature of the appliance malfunction.

steps.what: Customer reports the fault, appliance type and model number
Office planner takes the call and writes the work order
Repairer refers to the work order before the visit
Repairer calls the customer ahead to ask for the model number and symptoms
Repairer talks to the customer on site to establish the nature of the appliance malfunction

tasks.design: Customers can book a repair on the company's web form: appliance type, a photo of the type plate, symptoms picked from a list and a free comment, with about the effort of a phone call. The form creates the work order, which the planner checks and schedules, and the repairer sees it with photo and model number in the app, so calls ahead are only needed when something is missing. Talking with the customer on site stays the same.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults were described by phone and model numbers were rarely known before the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Web booking forms with photo upload that create work orders.
tasks.still_hard: Customers who describe the fault vaguely.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the one question that pins down the fault.
tasks.altitude: Fewer calls ahead; the conversation on site stays.

reach.learn: Whether web bookings cut phone time.

evidence.claim: Work order platforms run from quote to invoice for installers.
A fibre operator reports about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail and entry (vendor case).

assumptions: Boundary: establishing the fault before and at the visit; the repair is outside.

Input contract for s4: model number from the type plate photo and symptoms entered by customers on the web form (s1) with about the effort of a call; about 60% of customers book that way; the rest still phone; s4 is priced at that share.
The conversation on site keeps its full time; customer and planner time are outside the repairer's savings.
unknowns: Share of customers willing to book online.
research_questions: Do first-visit fixes rise when the model is known?

incremental.description: Repairer looks at the type plate photo before the visit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older customers who phone; high: younger customers who book online with photos.

tasks.short: Find the manual and schematic for the model, refer to schematic drawings, product manuals and troubleshooting guides to diagnose and repair problems, and look up known fixes.

steps.what: Repairer finds the right manual and schematic drawings for the model
Repairer refers to schematic drawings, product manuals and troubleshooting guides to diagnose and repair

loop.input: The repairer's question, the model number and the service documents for that model the company is licensed to use.
loop.output: The relevant troubleshooting steps and the schematic page, quoted from the documents.
loop.check: Every answer must quote the document and page for this model number, or it says nothing was found; the repairer reads the quoted page before acting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Manuals run to hundreds of pages and the index rarely matches the symptom.

steps.what: Repairer looks up known fixes and service bulletins

tasks.design: The model number in the work order opens the manual, schematic and service bulletins for that model from the manufacturers' service portals the company has access to, instead of the repairer searching per brand. An answer desk over those documents quotes the troubleshooting steps and schematic page for a question; the repairer reads the page and decides. The company's own history of fixes per model is searchable in the work order app.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals were searched per brand portal or in paper binders in the van.
tasks.enabler_now: Service portals by model number, and answer desks that quote document pages.
tasks.still_hard: Models with poor or missing service documentation.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a fix that is not in any manual.
tasks.altitude: Less searching; diagnosis stays with the repairer.

reach.learn: Whether part numbers from schematics reduce wrong orders.

evidence.claim: Maintenance apps draft procedures that are reviewed before use; generated content needs checking.
Manufacturers' service documents may only be used within the company's licence terms.

assumptions: Boundary: finding and reading service information for a repair; the repair work is outside.

Input contract for s1: the model number in the work order (from the customer's type plate photo or the repairer's scan) and access to manufacturers' service portals for about 70% of brands repaired; other brands are searched as today; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: only service documents the company is licensed to use are loaded.
The repairer's diagnosis keeps most of its time.
unknowns: Which brands give portal access to independent repairers.

already_counted.description: Repairer reads the quoted page before acting on an answer.

incremental.description: Repairer adds new fixes to the company's history.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many brands without portal access; high: a few big brands with full service portals.
